subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw core add a jobs.d/declarative cron file sync surface, or should this remain a ClawHub/plugin workflow using declarationKey and cron APIs?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally make SQLite the cron runtime store, while this request adds a file-backed declarative input path with compatibility, deletion, and path-trust semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Keep as product design item
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer chooses the core-vs-plugin direction and the compatibility/security contract.

options.title: Route to ClawHub sync plugin
options.body: Close or redirect if maintainers decide a directory-to-cron sync plugin is sufficient with gateway_start, cron_changed, cron.add, and declarationKey.

options.title: Sponsor core declarative sync
options.body: Approve a core design that documents import/sync semantics, preserves SQLite runtime state, and covers doctor, docs, and focused cron tests.

recommendation.title: Keep as product design item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer chooses the core-vs-plugin direction and the compatibility/security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent cron SQLite migration and storage refactor history makes steipete the clearest routing candidate for the storage/product boundary decision.
